label: Inputs 3/x/m/l/h/z at the start of the sequence (t<=1)
explanation: Fires mostly when the input is one of 3, x, m, l, h (z weaker) and strongly favours the first one or two steps of the sequence. At t=0 it fires only on these tokens (precision 1.0 for t==0 & token), and t=0 alone carries 40% of the activation mass. The same tokens later in the original phase or the copy phase fire much less reliably (about 20% rate overall). About 46% of the mass is not covered by this rule. That remainder is spread out: the delimiter step (11% of mass, including the largest activations when the sequence starts with u/o/2), and copy steps that output u, o or 2 (low precision). Neither of these gives a clean clause. Activation decays with position in the original phase and is roughly zero for orig_idx>=5. Dev split: P=0.77, R=0.48, mass recall 0.54.
